title: MRI Data Acquisition Protocol
author: Lukas Snoek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ypwfvpe

steps.title: Complete MRI screening form
steps.instruction: Have the participant fill out the MRI safety screening form before entering the operating room, verify the signature, discuss tattoos, surgeries or other safety issues, consult Tinka or Lukas if unsure, and if any doubt send the participant home; never place the subject‑identifier on the form or any other document, keep personal data separate for 48 h, then after the experiment place the completed form in the designated mailbox.

steps.title: Obtain GP informed consent
steps.instruction: Ask the participant to complete the General Practitioner Informed Consent with name and contact details of their GP; if the participant has no GP or refuses to provide the information they may not take part; after the scan, if no abnormalities were found place the form in the blue confidential container upstairs for destruction.

steps.title: Obtain study-specific consent
steps.instruction: Provide the participant with the study‑specific informed consent approved by the university’s ethical committee and have them read and sign it.

steps.title: Provide participant information folder
steps.instruction: Give the participant the MRI information folder (even if they are late) and ensure they understand the general MRI procedure and the specifics of your experiment.

steps.title: Verify BIDS exam card naming
steps.instruction: If you will use the centre’s QC/pre‑processing service, check that every exam‑card name follows BIDS conventions: replace all placeholders (e.g., (this_is_a_placeholder)), use the pattern task‑<taskname>_run‑<nr>_bold (e.g., task‑workingmemory_run‑1_bold), ensure each card has a unique name and that the run‑<nr> field is correctly incremented.

steps.title: Create new examination entry
steps.instruction: On the scan‑computer open Patients → New administration and fill in:

substeps.instruction: Patient name*: BIDS‑compatible subject identifier (e.g., sub‑01)
Registration ID*: same as patient name
Date of birth: 01‑01‑1980 (dummy date for anonymity)
Gender: participant’s gender
Patient weight: weight from the screening form (used for SAR calculation)
Patient conditions: pregnant = No, implant = No
Medical alerts/allergies: leave empty
Examination name: project identifier without spaces (e.g., ExampleExp)
Accession number: leave empty
Examination date: today
Referring Physician: PI of the project
Performing Physician: MR‑operator
Study Comments: leave empty
Allowed SAR mode: 1st Level

steps.title: Perform pre‑scan safety check
steps.instruction: Together with the participant, verify safety before entering the scanner room:

substeps.instruction: Shoes removed
Bra removed if under‑wired
Clothes are dry; provide sweatpants/sweatshirt if wet
Wear covering clothes (no shorts/skirts/tank tops)
All pockets emptied
Hair free of pins or clips
All jewelry, watches removed unless completely non‑metallic
Check participant’s clothing for ferromagnetic pieces and replace with provided garments if needed
Operator checks own pockets and ensures personal safety
Enter scanner room, close the door behind you
A magnetic field will be active; safety screening has been performed
The scanner is noisy; they will receive earplugs and headphones
They cannot speak during scans; an alarm button is provided for emergencies or to stop the scan
Communication will occur via intercom before the first scan and between scans
They should stay relaxed to minimise movement and improve data quality; remind them to move as little as possible between scans

steps.title: Export MRI data to local drive

substeps.instruction: Open Patients → Administration, locate the participant’s examination and double‑click it
Select all scans except SmartBrain, MPR‑SmartBrain, CoilSurveyScan, SenseRefScan, and B0_PreScan
Click Disk Files → choose Non‑DICOM Export (recommended)
Check ‘Use Scan Name’ and ‘Sort’ boxes
Select file format PAR‑REC (native Philips format with most metadata)
Set Destination to e:\dicom (or another local folder) and click Proceed
When export finishes, cut & paste the files from e:\dicom to your project export folder (e.g., Z:/fMRI Project ExampleExp)
Export immediately after scanning; MRI data are retained on the scanner only for two days, so verify that the export succeeded

steps.title: Transfer exported data to project folder
steps.instruction: Copy the exported files from the local drive to the shared project folder (fMRI Projects for UvA researchers or Dropbox for external researchers).

steps.title: Export experiment logfiles to project folder
steps.instruction: Move event‑files from the stimulus computer:

substeps.instruction: Exit testing mode by double‑clicking the green start button on the stimulus desktop (enables internet)
Map the network drive Z: → This PC → Map Network Drive, set folder to \\bigbrother.fmg.uva.nl\fmri_projects$ (or \Dropbox$), check ‘Reconnect at logon’ and ‘Connect using different credentials’
Enter credentials (prepend uva\ to your UvANetID for UvA staff)
Copy‑paste logfiles (e.g., C:\data\some_logfile.txt) to Z:\fMRI Project ExampleExp

steps.title: Handle physiology recordings (if any)
steps.instruction: If heart‑rate or respiration was recorded, copy the SCANPHYSLOG*.txt file from the scan‑computer to the export folder and rename it to BIDS‑compatible form:

substeps.instruction: sub-(identifier)[_ses-(identifier)]_task-(taskname)[_acq-(identifier)][_run-(nr)]_physio.txt
Replace the original scan identifier (usually _bold) with _physio

steps.title: Organize exported data in BIDS raw folder
steps.instruction: Structure the export folder as required for the automatic BIDS conversion:

substeps.instruction: Create a subfolder called raw inside the project folder
Inside raw, create a folder for each subject (e.g., sub‑01) and, if applicable, a session folder (e.g., ses‑01)
Place the PAR/REC files using the BIDS naming scheme (e.g., sub‑01_ses‑01_T1w.PAR, sub‑01_ses‑01_task‑Nback_acq‑SeqSense2Mm3_bold.PAR, etc.)
Do not create directories on the scan‑computer; use the scan‑assistant computer for folder creation
Every night at 11 pm the centre checks the export folders, copies new data to the server, runs BIDS conversion, QC and optional fmriprep; results appear in a bids/ sub‑directory within 24 h
If results are missing or incorrect, email Lukas

steps.title: Perform end‑of‑day cleanup (standard)
steps.instruction: When the day’s scanning is finished, complete:

substeps.instruction: Verify all MRI screening forms are complete, signed, and placed in the mailbox
Elevate the scanner‑room table
Close the current examination on the scan computer
Put fresh paper and two earplugs on the scanner table
Tidy the scanner and operating rooms (remove tape, used earplugs, etc.)
Lock the scanner‑room door and hang the key in the cabinet
Archive or discard all documents used during the experiment (consents, screening forms, etc.)
Log out of any websites or services on the scan‑assistant computer (e.g., Facebook, email)

steps.title: Perform end‑of‑day cleanup (last researcher)
steps.instruction: If you are the last researcher of the day (check Calpendo), in addition to the standard cleanup do:

substeps.instruction: Unplug the headcoil
Turn off the monitor in the scanner room (button next to stimulus computer)
Shut down the stimulus computer and the scan‑assistant computer (to the right of the scan computer)
Restart the scan computer (Start → Restart) and then turn its monitor off
Turn off any cubicle computers if used
Close the operating‑room door after leaving
Turn off all lights and activate the building alarm

steps.title: Apply BIDS‑compatible subject identifiers
steps.instruction: When creating the examination, use zero‑padded subject IDs (e.g., sub‑01, sub‑09, sub‑10) and follow the BIDS pattern:

substeps.instruction: sub‑[condition](number)[_ses-(identifier)]
Condition is optional (e.g., CON or TRE for between‑subject designs)
Number is mandatory and zero‑padded (01, 02 …)
Session identifier is optional (e.g., _ses‑01)
Examples: sub‑01, sub‑CON01_ses‑1, sub‑TRE20_ses‑2
